title: Safari Notebook: LLM reads and action list
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal capture after skimming a pile of papers and blog posts on long-context inference, kv compression, and latency-aware batching. Want a short prioritized list of experiments we can try on the small cluster before giving anything to solutions-eng.

Top-line takeaways (first pass):
- KV-compression looks promising for long-session cost reductions, but evictions + reconstruction cost matter more than raw on-disk size.
- Latency-aware batching (adaptive batch windows based on request percentile) is an easy low-risk lever to test in our routing layer.
- MoE/conditional compute at inference still expensive for small/medium models due to routing overhead; better for very large sparse setups.
- There are several pragmatic microtricks in the blogs (prefix-caching heuristics, delta-encoding of hidden states) that are often omitted from papers; worth trying.

Reads summarized (snappy):
1) "Compressing KV caches for 1M token sessions" (blog, Oct 2026)
   - Idea: lossy transform (quant+PCA-like) per-layer per-head, store reduced vectors + small corrections for hot entries.
   - My take: cheap to implement as a shim in our cache layer; could be toggled per-customer.
   - Risk: recompute cost if we need to restore exact keys for attention — need fallback for safety-critical prompts.

2) "Latency-aware batching: smoothing tail latencies" (conference talk notes, Nov 2026)
   - Idea: use micro-deadlines per request tied to percentiles (p50/p95) and opportunistic small batching for p95.
   - My take: we can prototype by instrumenting per-route timers in dev cluster and running a simulated request mix. Low infra changes.

3) "Sparse routing in inference: lessons learned" (arXiv + appendix, Sep 2026)
   - Idea: conditional layers with expert selection; big wins only for huge MoE models and very high throughput shapes.
   - My take: deprioritize unless we target enterprise with giant models; complexity > benefit for now.

Notes and fragments:
- Idea sketch: KV-tiering. Keep "hot" exact float32 KV entries in GPU, move compressed LP entries to host/persistent cache. Promote/demote based on recent access count. (Sketch: maintain LRU + access counter, periodic compaction job)
- How to measure correctness: run a small deterministic suite (5 prompts per category) and compare logits / next-token probs after compression and after full restore. Threshold: <0.5% change in top-1 accuracy for non-critical tasks.
- Economics: compressing to 1/8 size might cut cost on long sessions by ~20% when cache hits > 30% of tokens. Need spreadsheet sim.
- Quick code plan: add a CacheSerializer interface: to_bytes(layer_idx, head_idx, kv_tensor) -> bytes; backends: raw, quant8, pca-lite. Hook this into existing cache checkpoint path.

Experimental priorities (next 3 weeks):
1) Microbench: implement quant8 serializer + roundtrip test (owner: me).
   - success criteria: roundtrip MSE < 1e-5 on val set, CPU decompress < 1.5x current latency cost on small blob sizes.
2) Routing sim: add latency-aware batching knob behind feature flag and replay historical traffic on dev cluster (owner: Hana).
   - success criteria: p95 reduction >= 10% for route X without p50 increase > 5%.
3) KV-tiering sim: offline trace replay to compute hit rates with a simulated cache (owner: Lina).
   - success criteria: identify a realistic policy that yields >25% memory reduction for top-10% longest sessions.

Open questions / quick risks:
- Can we guarantee determinism for evals when storing compressed KVs? Need a canonical test harness.
- How do we surface fidelity regressions to product? Suggest a small warning metric in Console + rollout gating.
- Legal/security: if we keep compressed cache on host storage, does that change PII requirements? Ping security/compliance.

Links I should read next (shortlist):
- "Efficient Long Context Inference" (ICLR workshop, 2026) — focus on kernels and attention asymptotics.
- "Practical KV compression for LLMs" (company blog with code samples) — try the code sample.
- Slack thread: #kv-cache-magic (Hana posted microbench results Nov 18)

Todo (near term):
- [ ] Create GH PR prototype for CacheSerializer interface (branch: noam/kv-serializer)
- [ ] Run small roundtrip bench and post numbers in GH issue GH-4123
- [ ] Draft a Console metric proposal: "KV fidelity delta" with 3 thresholds (info/warn/block)
- [ ] Ask Legal about persisted compressed KVs (short note to security@redwood)
- [ ] Sync with Hana on latency-aware batching sim (10–15 min async)

Meeting notes (2026-12-02 sprint sync):
- Lina: has traffic traces for two customers with long sessions; will share sanitized subset.
- Hana: already instrumented latencies per-route, can wire sim to our dev cluster.
- Prod: prefer feature-flagged rollout with gradual weight and rollback hooks.

Rough timeline (working):
- Week 1: prototype serializer + local roundtrip tests
- Week 2: run trace replays, measure mem/cost delta, iterate compressor params
- Week 3: small feature-flagged run for one internal route, measure user-visible latency/cost

Random brain-dump (keep brief):
- Could prefix-sparsify keys by hashing on token types to reduce stored entries (only keep noun/prop tokens?) — silly but maybe for domain-specific copilots.
- Consider storing delta-encoded KV diffs for sequential tokens in very long streams to exploit locality.

If you read this and want to help: ping me (Noam) or drop a quick note in GH-issue #4123. I'll try to keep this notebook tidy but it will stay messy for a bit.

Signed-off: Noam
